chapter: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
title: Ella backs him in a dispute over his recording check
summary: Road manager Tim Gale tried to deduct the Decca record date money for his borrowed drums; Clarke refused to go on stage and Ella refused too until he was paid.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: No, no. Well, I had a hassle with him because Bill [Mather] was a drum -- had a drum store, and he was a very good friend of mine. And I needed some drums to join Ella, you know, some decent drums to play. So he let me have a set of drums, and then Tim Gale was supposed to take out so much a week. So we come down during the week and we make a record date with Ella at the Decca Studios. Bob Stevens.
: Yeah.

A wonderful guy. And we do this date, so we go back to Boston and in a few days all the musicians received a check, and it was Tommy Fulford, Beverly, and myself, and (Inaudible) So I said receive a check "Where's my check." He said, "You don't get a check." I said, "Listen, you're taking it out of my salary if you're talking about the drums. It has nothing to do with the recording date. You're not supposed to take my recording date. You're supposed to take the money out --,"
So much --
So much a week. I said, "My recording date, I must have it."
Yeah.

So he says, "Well, we have to take it out." So I said, "Well, I'm not going on." So Ella says, "Well, if Kenny's not going on, I'm not going on either." So they had kind of a billiard room in the back, so we were starting to play billiards, and I said, "I'm not going on until you give me my check." So the manager of the Cocoanut Grove, he was saying, "Well, listen now, you must go on." And she said, "Well, we're having a little difficulty. Now, I'll let you know." He says, "Well, okay, but I mean you have to go on soon, huh, because it's time." So she says, "Kenny, are you going on?" I said, "No, Ella, I'm not going on until I get my check," call her Sis, you know. I said, "Sis, I'm not going on until that cat gives me my check. He has nothing to do with my record

check." So Ella says, 'Well, I can't go on without you. I'm not going up there without drums, without a rhythm section.' You know. So she stayed back in the restaurant with me. So finally, Tim Gale comes back. He says, 'How about it, Kenny?' I said, 'I told you, Tim, I'm not going on until you give me my record check, because it has nothing to do with the drums. Now, please give me my check if you want us to play.' So he hemmed and hawed and hemmed and hawed and I said, 'Okay, you can hem and haw all you want, but I'm not going on.' So then the manager comes out. He was kind of furious now, you know, because we had waited. This had been about 25 minutes.
And at the Cocoanut Grove, too.

Yeah. He's kind of -- so he says, 'Well, listen, somebody has to do something because this band has to go on now.' So Tim said -- and I said, 'No. When I said no I mean no.' So Ella says, 'Why don't you Give him his check.' You have it in your pocket.' So he said, 'Okay.' And he gave me my record check and so we go on. I said what are you doing it at first, because you're going to take the money out this week when we finish, so why do you want to take my record check?
Yeah, it's stupid. Very stupid.
So that was one time Ella was on my side, you know.
Yeah.
She stuck with me right through it. And that's --
She's a good person. Don't you think she is?
Yeah. She is.
She's a human being.
That's right. She understood what was going on and she didn't think it was fair.
No.
So she said, 'If Kenny stays off I'm not going on there.'
Yeah, that's right.
So there it was.
